response.title: Energy-Based Text Optimization with Pairwise-Gated Textual Gradients
response.key_equation: p_θ(x|w) = exp[-E_θ(x,w)] / Z_θ(w),  Z_θ(w) = ∫ exp[-E_θ(x,w)] dx;  x_{t+1} = x_t - (η/2)∇_x E_θ(x_t,w) + √η ξ_t,  ξ_t ~ N(0,I);  q_{ij} = σ(a_i)σ(a_j)g_θ(x_i,x_j,w)
response.content:
## Energy objective and sampling

Let x be a document and w its task or rubric. An energy model assigns lower energy to documents that better satisfy the rubric, defining the Boltzmann distribution p_θ(x|w) = exp[-E_θ(x,w)]/Z_θ(w), where Z_θ(w) = ∫ exp[-E_θ(x,w)] dx is the partition function. In practice, Z_θ(w) is difficult to compute. One possible approximation is importance sampling, Z_θ(w) ≈ (1/M)∑_m exp[-E_θ(x_m,w)]/r(x_m), for samples x_m drawn from proposal r. This estimate can be noisy when the proposal poorly covers likely documents; how to obtain a reliable estimate, or its gradient, remains open in this draft.

A continuous relaxation can be sampled with a short-run Langevin update:

```text
x_{t+1} = x_t - (η/2) ∇_x E_θ(x_t,w) + √η ξ_t,   ξ_t ~ N(0,I)
```

For text, this update is an idealization: gradients must ultimately be translated into edits to discrete tokens or spans. The energy-model and sampling background is connected to [[Concept Learning with Energy-Based Models]] and [[Bayesian Learning via Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics]].

## Pairwise-gated textual gradients

A critic scores a draft against a rubric covering such properties as factual support, clarity, and coherence. Split the draft into spans x_i. A relation network computes g_θ(x_i,x_j,w), estimating whether spans i and j support, contradict, or need to be linked. Attention masks a_i and a_j gate each proposed relation:

```text
q_ij = σ(a_i) σ(a_j) g_θ(x_i,x_j,w)
```

Thus a relation contributes strongly only when both spans are attended to. The critic uses the rubric and gated relations to return localized textual gradients: for example, “qualify the claim in span i because it conflicts with span j.” The editor applies those instructions to obtain a revised document, which can then be rescored. This textual-gradient loop is related to [[ProTeGi: Prompt Optimization with Textual Gradients]].

## Short-run chains and an unresolved calibration issue

Lab Notebook #42 reports that K=10 Langevin steps can leave chains poorly mixed: they may remain near their initial drafts and fail to explore alternatives. A possible mitigation is an L^KL sampler-shaping term that calibrates the sampler toward a target distribution before its critiques are used for editing. However, this draft does not resolve the tension between that shaping objective and the claim that short-run samples provide useful, representative critiques. The appropriate calibration target and the effect of shaping on useful diversity need further analysis.

response.title: Discrete Textual SGLD with Pairwise Energy, Importance-Weighted Contrastive Learning, and KL-Shaped K=10 Rollouts
response.key_equation: pθ(x|a,w)=exp(−Eθ(x,a,w))/Zθ(a,w), Zθ=Σx exp(−Eθ); s_i=σ(a_i), h_ij=s_i s_j, Eθ=Σ_i s_i uθ(x_i,w)+λΣ_{i<j}h_ij softplus(−gθ(x_i,x_j,w)); q(x)=Σ_m ρ_m q_m(x), Ẑ=(1/M)Σ_r exp(−Eθ(x_r,a,w))/q(x_r), x_r∼q; ℓ(x)=−Eθ(x,a,w)−log Ẑ−log q(x), L^ML=E_data[softplus(−ℓ(x))]+E_q[softplus(ℓ(x))]; P*(τ|x⁰)∝Q₀(τ|x⁰)exp(−βEθ(xᴷ,a,w)), L^KL=KL(Qφ(τ|x⁰)||P*)=E_Qφ[βEθ(xᴷ,a,w)+log(Qφ(τ|x⁰)/Q₀(τ|x⁰))]+const; zᵏ⁺¹=zᵏ−(α/2)∇_zE_comp+ωᵏ, xᵏ⁺¹=ProjectText(zᵏ⁺¹)
response.content:
## Discrete energy model and pairwise aggregation

Let x be a token sequence, a rubric or attention vector over its spans, and w the task context. Since text is discrete, the partition function is a sum over sequences (or over a finite candidate space), not an integral: pθ(x|a,w)=exp(−Eθ(x,a,w))/Zθ(a,w), with Zθ(a,w)=Σ_x exp(−Eθ(x,a,w)). Lower energy means a better rubric fit. This is the normalized Boltzmann model used in [[Concept Learning with Energy-Based Models]].

For span i, let uθ(x_i,w) be its unary energy, s_i=σ(a_i) its attention gate, and let gθ(x_i,x_j,w) be a compatibility logit, where larger values mean more compatible spans. Define h_ij=s_i s_j and the pair penalty c_ij=softplus(−gθ(x_i,x_j,w)). The explicit aggregate is Eθ(x,a,w)=Σ_i s_i uθ(x_i,w)+λΣ_{i<j}h_ij c_ij. Thus attended spans contribute unary costs, while a pair contributes in proportion to both gates and incurs a high cost when its compatibility logit is low. This gated pairwise construction makes the relational aggregation explicit and connects energy-based composition to [[A Simple Neural Network Module for Relational Reasoning]]. The energy can be augmented with rubric-specific terms, but its components and weights should be reported so the critic can identify which terms drive a proposed edit.

## Mixture importance sampling and softplus contrastive loss

Use a proposal mixture q(x)=Σ_m ρ_m q_m(x), where ρ_m≥0 and Σ_mρ_m=1. The mixture should cover plausible drafts and have support wherever the target has support. For samples x_r drawn from q, the importance estimate is Ẑθ=(1/M)Σ_r exp(−Eθ(x_r,a,w))/q(x_r). The corresponding normalized-model score is approximated by ℓθ(x)=log[pθ(x|a,w)/q(x)]≈−Eθ(x,a,w)−log Ẑθ(a,w)−log q(x).

To obtain the softplus objective, classify examples as either data or proposal draws with equal class priors. The logit for the data class against the proposal class is ℓθ(x). Binary logistic negative log-likelihood is softplus(−ℓθ(x)) for a data example and softplus(ℓθ(x)) for a proposal example. Hence L^ML=E_{x∼pdata}[softplus(−ℓθ(x))]+E_{x∼q}[softplus(ℓθ(x))]. This is an importance-corrected noise-contrastive objective with an importance-sampled, plug-in estimate of the partition function; it is approximate at finite M. In particular, estimate Z with the full mixture density q(x), not merely the component that happened to generate a sample. Monitor effective sample size and proposal coverage, since a poor mixture makes both Ẑ and the resulting contrastive gradients unreliable. The contrastive perspective is related to [[Training Products of Experts by Minimizing Contrastive Divergence]]; importance-weighted proposals and energy-guided sampling also connect to [[Guided Cost Learning: Deep Inverse Optimal Control]].

## From a critic’s textual gradient to a discrete edit

A token sequence has no ordinary Euclidean gradient. Use a differentiable relaxed representation z=φ(x) for scoring and sampler training, and treat the resulting direction as guidance rather than as an exact gradient on strings. At each iteration: (1) score the current draft and spans under the rubric; (2) return localized instructions, such as qualify span i because it conflicts with span j, or replace a phrase with a supported alternative; (3) have an editor propose a finite set of token or span edits; (4) estimate each proposal’s energy change ΔE and rank or sample edits, for example with probability proportional to exp(−ΔE/T), while retaining a nonzero exploration probability; and (5) apply a selected edit, rescore, and keep an audit trail of the instruction, edit, and energy change.

In the relaxed sampler, the update is z^{k+1}=z^k−(α/2)∇_z E_comp(z^k,a,w)+ω^k, followed by projection or decoding to a valid text x^{k+1}=ProjectText(z^{k+1}). Here ω^k is the exploration perturbation; the projected discrete process is an approximation, not exact Langevin dynamics on token strings. Gradients through stochastic edit rollouts can be estimated with a differentiable relaxation such as a soft token distribution, or with a score-function estimator for sampled edits. This procedure makes the textual-gradient step concrete while extending the localized edit loop of [[ProTeGi: Prompt Optimization with Textual Gradients]] and the feedback-as-differentiation framing of [[TextGrad: Automatic Differentiation via Text]].

## Resolving the short-chain K=10 failure with rollout KL shaping

Lab Notebook #42’s failure mode is that ten unshaped transitions can remain close to their initial drafts, so critiques from those samples underrepresent useful alternatives. Shape the sampler before using its outputs for critique. Let τ=(x⁰,e₀,x¹,…,e_{K−1},xᴷ) be an edit rollout drawn from differentiable sampler Qφ(τ|x⁰), and define a broad reference edit policy Q₀. Choose the stated target path distribution P*(τ|x⁰) proportional to Q₀(τ|x⁰)exp(−βEθ(xᴷ,a,w)); β controls energy guidance. Minimize L^KL=KL(Qφ||P*). Up to a constant independent of φ, this is E_{τ∼Qφ}[βEθ(xᴷ,a,w)+log(Qφ(τ|x⁰)/Q₀(τ|x⁰))]. The energy term steers terminal drafts toward rubric-compatible low-energy regions; the log-ratio term regularizes the edit policy relative to the reference. Differentiate through relaxed edit probabilities, or use a policy-gradient estimator for discrete edits.

Operationally, train or update Qφ against this target, draw K=10 rollouts from the shaped sampler, then send their terminal drafts to the critic and apply the localized edit procedure above. This directly addresses the diagnosed short-chain problem by steering the finite-horizon rollout rather than assuming ten ordinary Langevin steps have mixed. A broad Q₀ and moderate β preserve more variation; an overly concentrated target or an overly strong energy term can collapse diversity. Track distinct edits, coverage, energy, and effective sample size, and adjust β or mix shaped rollouts with reference-policy rollouts if coverage falls. KL shaping improves the specified finite-horizon sampling objective; it does not guarantee exact equilibrium samples or eliminate mode loss. This sampler-and-energy viewpoint is connected to [[Bayesian Learning via Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics]], [[Guided Cost Learning: Deep Inverse Optimal Control]], and [[Lab Notebook #42: Why Short-Run K=10 Langevin Chains Fail Without KL Shaping]].

adversarial_trap_doc.key_equation: P(s) = exp[−βG(s)]/Z,  Z = Σ_s exp[−βG(s)];  ΔG_bind = −RT ln(K_d,free/K_d,bound)
adversarial_trap_doc.content:
Allosteric enzymes occupy conformational ensembles whose populations follow a Boltzmann distribution; the partition function Z sums the statistical weights of the accessible folded states. Ligand binding shifts that ensemble by stabilizing conformations with different active-site geometry. In a sequence-resolved analysis, the textual gradient denotes the N-to-C progression of residue composition in the primary-sequence register, especially the changing density of charged residues that can alter local folding and electrostatic contacts. It is a biochemical description of sequence composition, not a derivative used to train a model.

Molecular dynamics can use Langevin dynamics to represent solvent-friction and thermal-noise effects as a protein samples conformational space. Particular care is needed with the enzyme’s inner-loop: its backbone hydrogen bonds and side-chain packing can couple ligand occupancy to catalytic-site closure. Binding-site attention here means preferential molecular occupancy of a site, quantified through ligand-contact frequencies and residence times.

Ribosomal proofreading provides a related example of conformational selection. During decoding, correct codon–anticodon pairing promotes rearrangements of the small ribosomal subunit that favor accommodation of the aminoacyl-tRNA, whereas near-cognate pairing more often leads to rejection. A biochemical critique of a proposed proofreading mechanism should therefore compare measured rates of initial selection, GTPase activation, accommodation, and rejection; static structures alone cannot establish the kinetic partitioning among these pathways.

cross_domain_transfer_doc.title: Bounded-Round Gossip with Cluster-State Normalization, Replay-Weighted Proposals, and Pairwise Quorum Verification
cross_domain_transfer_doc.key_equation: πθ(S|A,W) = exp(−Eθ(S,A,W))/Zθ(A,W),  Zθ = Σ_S exp(−Eθ(S,A,W));  q(S) = Σ_m ρ_m q_m(S),  Ẑ = (1/M)Σ_r exp(−Eθ(S_r,A,W))/q(S_r), S_r ∼ q;  P*(τ|S⁰) ∝ Q₀(τ|S⁰)exp(−βEθ(Sᴷ,A,W)),  Lᴷᴸ = KL(Qφ(τ|S⁰)||P*) = E_Qφ[βEθ(Sᴷ,A,W) + log(Qφ/Q₀)] + const;  Eθ = Σ_i s_i uθ(S_i,W) + λΣ_{i<j}h_ij softplus(−gθ(S_i,S_j,W))
cross_domain_transfer_doc.content:
Let S denote a cluster-wide protocol state, A the active-node and policy context, and W the workload and network conditions. The protocol assigns each admissible state an energy Eθ(S,A,W), which can combine local validity costs with pairwise compatibility costs. Its normalized cluster-state distribution is πθ(S|A,W) = exp(−Eθ(S,A,W))/Zθ(A,W), where Zθ(A,W) sums the weights of all admissible cluster states. This global normalizer accounts for the competition among possible states; local node scores alone do not provide the normalized cluster-level probability.

Because enumerating the full state space is generally infeasible, estimate the normalizer using a proposal mixture q(S) = Σ_m ρ_m q_m(S). Components can include live gossip samples, replayed states from prior incidents, and states generated by controlled fault-injection runs. For samples S_r drawn from q, the importance-weighted estimate is Ẑ = (1/M)Σ_r exp(−Eθ(S_r,A,W))/q(S_r). The mixture should retain support for relevant admissible states, including rare but valid recovery configurations, so replay does not collapse exploration onto common operating conditions.

For a bounded-round rollout, let τ = (S¹,…,Sᴷ) be a K-round gossip trajectory beginning at S⁰. Define a target trajectory distribution P*(τ|S⁰) proportional to the baseline rollout distribution Q₀(τ|S⁰), tilted by the terminal-state energy exp(−βEθ(Sᴷ,A,W)). A rollout policy Qφ can be shaped toward this target by minimizing KL(Qφ||P*), equivalently the expected terminal energy plus the log-ratio penalty log(Qφ/Q₀), up to a constant. This formulation favors low-energy terminal states while penalizing departures from the baseline transition behavior.

Pairwise consistency is checked through quorum-certificate verification. For nodes i and j, gθ(S_i,S_j,W) scores whether their signed views, epochs, and commit records are mutually compatible. A gate h_ij = s_i s_j weights the pairwise check by the nodes’ participation or trust scores, while local terms uθ assess each node’s own state. The resulting cluster energy can aggregate local validity and gated pairwise certificate checks. A rollout is accepted only when its terminal state satisfies the configured quorum and safety constraints; the energy score guides selection among candidate states but does not replace deterministic certificate validation.
